title: Chapter 3
content:
The duffel bag unzipped on the floor was stuffed to the brim with stacks of crisp greenbacks. As Wang Han sorted and bundled the bills, his gaze drifted over to Jakyeong, who was sitting at the dining table. Ever since they’d gotten back, Jakyeong had been staring intently at a single photograph—the new hit handed down directly from Dmitri.

"You're really going to take this?"

Jakyeong didn't answer right away.

The man in the photo wore a tailored black suit and a pitch-black tie, his expression unreadable, almost vacant. He looked like he belonged on the cover of a high-end Western magazine—or, more accurately, an ad for designer underwear. His features were remarkably sharp for an East Asian, chiseled and dripping with raw testosterone. But it was his eyes that caught the light: deep-set, cold, and utterly ruthless.

Wang Han pushed himself up from his chair and walked over, leaning over the table. "I asked if you're taking it."

Jakyeong rotated the photo so Wang Han could get a better look. "Good-looking, isn't he? Makes you almost excited to put him down."

"If you say so."

"Says here he's twenty-nine. Doesn't he look older? Man aged like milk."

"So you're doing it?"

Jakyeong nodded cleanly. "Got to. It’s ten times our usual rate."

Wang Han pulled out a chair and sat down, his expression darkening into a serious scowl. "I don't like it. Taking out a mark is one thing, but you're supposed to break into his house and steal something from his safe, too."

Predictably, a payout that huge came with heavy strings attached. It wasn't a standard, clean assassination. After putting a bullet in the man's head, Jakyeong had to crack a hidden safe and retrieve a specific item to complete the contract.

Wang Han picked up the photo, studying the face closely. He'd already called in a few favors to pull a background check.

The mark’s father was Kang Hoon—a legendary underworld boss who used to rule Sewon-pa, one of South Korea's most notorious criminal syndicates. Kang Hoon had legitimized the syndicate by marrying a politician's daughter, expanding his empire into legitimate corporate enterprises. Naturally, behind the squeaky-clean corporate front, he still reigned supreme as the undisputed king of the underworld.

Since then, the old man had been married twice more, fathering three sons and a daughter. The sons all managed various arms of the conglomerate, while the daughter was a surgeon. And of the three brothers, the prime candidate to inherit the entire criminal empire was the man in the photo: Kang Il-hyun.

Having spent a lifetime dealing with all sorts of degenerates in this business, Wang Han could read a man just by looking at his face. Il-hyun's aura alone screamed dangerous, but more than that, Wang Han’s gut was sounding the alarm. Walk away from this one.

On top of that, intelligence indicated this wasn't the first hit ordered on Kang Il-hyun. Every previous attempt had failed catastrophically. Not a single assassin had made it out alive.

Yet, as usual, Jakyeong remained completely unbothered. "Those guys were amateurs. I'm the best."

"I know you are," Wang Han said softly. "But if things go sideways... what then?"

"Then I die."

"Don't say it so casually. What about your dream?"

At the word dream, Jakyeong went quiet.

His plan had always been to retire the moment he turned thirty. He'd already picked out an island for his golden years—an uninhabited, secluded rock far away from civilization. Given how many enemies he’d made over the years, off-grid isolation felt like the only place he'd ever truly get some peace. He envisioned finding a sweet girl, building a house, having a kid, going fishing, and living a quiet, domestic life. And he made a sacred vow to himself: he’d never, ever teach his kid how to pull a trigger.

"I'll worry about retirement after I get back," Jakyeong said, shaking off the moment. "First, I deal with this guy."

He pulled out his silver Zippo, flicking the wheel to set fire to the photo and the briefing files. As the flame swallowed the paper, Kang Il-hyun’s chiseled face contorted in the heat, making him look almost furious.

I wonder if he’ll make that same face when he dies, Jakyeong thought, a faint, cold smirk touching his lips. Can't wait to find out.

He tossed the burning paper into the wastebasket. Within seconds, the photo turned to a pile of dark, lifeless ash.

The sleek black sedan pulled up to the retreat in Yangpyeong after a two-hour drive, just as the sun was dipping below the horizon. The luxurious villa belonged to Chairman Kang, but it was mostly used as a personal playground for his youngest son, Kang Seok-joo, and his degenerate friends.

As the heavy iron gates swung open, several men were visible clearing out the perimeter around the outdoor pool. They were scrubbing chunks of shredded flesh and dark bloodstains off the concrete, but the moment they saw Il-hyun's car, they instantly straightened up and bowed deeply. Incidents like this happened all the time here, and cleaning up the gore was just part of their job description.

"Keep up the good work," Il-hyun said smoothly as he stepped out.

Before he even reached the grand stone steps leading to the front doors, muffled screams echoed from inside, accompanied by the violent shattering of glass and furniture. It didn't take a genius to figure out what was happening. The kid was still high out of his mind, flying into a psychotic rage.

Il-hyun glanced back at Tae-soo over his shoulder. "If I killed that brat right now, do you think the Old Man would shed a tear?"

Tae-soo kept his mouth shut. Whether Il-hyun was joking or deadly serious, Tae-soo's job was simply to execute whatever command followed.

"Nah... not yet," Il-hyun murmured, answering his own question. "He needs to die with the Old Man. That’s the only way I’ll actually enjoy it."

A faint, chilling smile flickered across Il-hyun's face before vanishing as quickly as it came.

He pushed the double doors open and stepped inside. As expected, the foyer was absolute carnage. The stench of copper and fresh blood hung thick in the air, mixed with the sickening, metallic odor of torn flesh.

Il-hyun took a deep, deliberate breath through his nose. Ah. What a lovely smell.

With every step he took, the soles of his polished leather shoes made a wet, sticky squelch against the blood-soaked hardwood.

The low-level goons huddled inside scrambled out of the way the second they spotted Il-hyun, revealing Kang Seok-joo in the center of the room. Covered head-to-toe in blood, the youngest brother was wildly swinging an ice pick like a feral animal.

"Get back! Get the fuck away from me, you pieces of shit!" Seok-joo shrieked, his eyes bloodshot and unfocused. "You wanna die?! Do you have any idea who I am?!"

Since you clearly forgot who you are and where you stand, Il-hyun thought, I suppose I’ll have to educate you.

Il-hyun closed the distance in three long strides. Seok-joo panicked, thrusting the ice pick wildly toward his face. "Fuck off! Back off, you motherfucker! I'll fucking kill you!"

Il-hyun leaned his head back just enough for the sharp steel tip to graze the air, caught Seok-joo’s wrist mid-air, and twisted it until the bone gave a sickening CRACK.

Seok-joo let out a high-pitched, ear-splitting shriek, but before he could even process the pain, Il-hyun snatched the ice pick from his limp hand and jammed the steel spike straight into his temple.

Gaggh!

The single blow cut off Seok-joo’s air completely. His eyes rolled into the back of his head, his knees buckling under him. But before he could collapse, Il-hyun grabbed him by the hair, yanking his head up to force eye contact. Then, with agonizing slowness, Il-hyun dragged the sharp point of the pick down Seok-joo's cheek.

The skin split open like overripe fruit, blood spurting out and spattering across Il-hyun’s pristine shoes.

Even through his drug-induced haze, the blinding pain was too much. Seok-joo began to tremble violently, shivering like a newborn calf.

"A... ugh... aagh!"

In sheer desperation, Seok-joo reached up to grab Il-hyun’s arm—only for a low, razor-sharp voice to slice through the air.

"Touch me, and the next one goes into your eyeball."

Seok-joo froze instantly, his mouth opening and closing silently. Tears of agony flooded his eyes, washing over the bloodshot whites. Finally, the fog cleared enough for him to see the man standing over him.

Il-hyun was smiling like a demon, his dark pupils sinking into an abyss of cold malice.

"B-Brother... p-please..."

"Can you see me clearly now?" Il-hyun asked softly.

"Y-Yes... yes..."

Il-hyun pressed down slightly, driving the tip of the ice pick deeper into the side of his skull. The sickening sound of steel scraping against bone echoed in the quiet room. Seok-joo couldn't even manage a scream, his mouth agape like a landed fish gasping for water.

Watching his half-brother writhe in absolute agony, a terrifying smile curved Il-hyun’s lips.

"Always maintain your manners when answering me. Understood?"

"Y... Yes..."

Satisfied, Il-hyun finally yanked the pick out of the bone and let go of Seok-joo's hair.

Seok-joo collapsed onto the bloodstained floor in a heap, gasping frantically for air. It wasn't just the physical agony that broke him—a wave of suffocating terror and visceral humiliation washed over him all at once.

As Il-hyun stood over the trembling mess, footsteps echoed from the entryway. He turned around, his cold expression instantly morphing into a warm, polite smile as he greeted the newcomer.

"You're late."

The white-haired man who stepped into the room was Director Yoon, the chief secretary to Seok-joo’s mother, Kim Sun-young. His eyes fell upon Seok-joo bleeding out on the floor, and his face instantly darkened.

"You went too far, Executive Director."

"I'll let Father give me the reprimand himself over dinner tomorrow," Il-hyun replied casually.

"Executive Director Kang."

"Speak."

"No matter the circumstances, physical violence between family members is unacceptable."

At the word family, one of Il-hyun's eyebrows arched up. The word left a foul taste in his mouth the more he chewed on it. Family. Family... Right. More like a nest of vipers.

Keeping his true feelings tucked safely behind a pleasant facade, Il-hyun slowly brought the bloody ice pick to his lips and licked the tip clean with his tongue.

Director Yoon’s eye twitched violently at the display.

Il-hyun swished the taste of his brother's blood around his mouth for a second before spitting it onto the floor with a loud Ptooey!

"How strange," Il-hyun murmured, tilting his head. "They always say blood is thicker than water... so why does his taste so watered down?"

"Executive Director," Yoon warned, his voice tight. "If you step out of line like this again—"

"If I do... what?"

Il-hyun’s gaze snapped up, locking onto Yoon with a freezing intensity.

Director Yoon froze mid-sentence. Instinctively taking a half-step back, he bowed his head low. "I spoke out of line. My apologies."

"See? I knew you were a quick study," Il-hyun chuckled smoothly, tossing the bloody ice pick onto the floor where it clattered against the tile. "Relax, Director Yoon. I'm just joking around. Don't take it to heart."

Director Yoon kept his head down, suppressing his utter revulsion. As much as he despised Kang Il-hyun, he couldn't openly defy him—not when Seok-joo had caused such a massive catastrophe this time. While none of the victims were dead, one of the kids Seok-joo stabbed happened to be the son of a high-ranking politician. Cleaning up this disaster fell entirely on Il-hyun’s shoulders, so his rage was somewhat justified.

"I'll be taking my leave now," Il-hyun said, turning toward the door. "Please ensure the cleanup is spotless. Just as you usually do."

Before stepping out, Il-hyun glanced back one last time. Seok-joo was still sitting on the floor, completely shell-shocked.

Il-hyun offered him an extraordinarily tender, benevolent smile.

"Look how cute and well-behaved you are when you're quiet," Il-hyun cooed softly. "Now you actually feel like my little brother."

Translator's Notes (A/N):

"Sewon-pa" (세원파): In South Korea, organized crime syndicates (often referred to as jo-pok) are typically named after the region, district, or foundational turf where they originated, followed by the suffix -pa (파, meaning 'faction' or 'clique').
"Gajot" (가좆): In the original Korean, Il-hyun thinks 가족 (family) and mentally twists it to 가좆. 좆 (joj) is a vulgar Korean slang term for male genitalia (equivalent to "dick" or "fuck"). He is making a derogatory pun on the concept of family—translated here conceptually as "nest of vipers."
